questions.text: If the ordinary generating function of a sequence [latex]\{a_{n}\}_{n=0}^{\infty} \;  is \;  \frac{1+z}{(1-z)^{3}}[/latex] then [latex]a_{3}-a_{0}[/latex] is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
[latex](1-z)^{-3}=\sum\binom{n+2}{2}z^n[/latex], so [latex]a_n=\binom{n+2}{2}+\binom{n+1}{2}[/latex].

[latex]a_3=10+6=16[/latex], [latex]a_0=1[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]a_3-a_0=15[/latex]

Answer: 15

questions.text: If a random variable X has a Poisson distribution with mean 5, then the expectation [latex]E[(X+2)^{2}][/latex] equals ______________.
questions.solution:
For Poisson, mean = variance = 5, so [latex]E[X^2]=5+25=30[/latex].

[latex]E[(X+2)^2]=E[X^2]+4E[X]+4=30+20+4=54[/latex]

Answer: 54

questions.text: In a [latex]B^{+}[/latex] tree, if the search -key value is 8 bytes long, the block size is 512 bytes and the block pointer size is 2 bytes, then maximum order of the [latex]B^{+}[/latex] tree is _______________.
questions.solution:
A node of order p has p block pointers and p [latex]-[/latex] 1 keys:
[latex]2p+8(p-1)\le512\Rightarrow10p\le520\Rightarrow p=52[/latex]

Answer: 52

questions.text:
A message is made up entirely of characters from the set X= {P,Q,R,S,T}. The table of probabilities for each of the characters is shown below:

If a message of 100 characters over X is encoded using Huffman coding, then the expected length of the encoded message in bits is_____
questions.solution:
Huffman: T (0.08) + R (0.17) = 0.25; S (0.19) + P (0.22) = 0.41; 0.25 + Q (0.34) = 0.59; 0.41 + 0.59.
Code lengths: Q 2, S 2, P 2, T 3, R 3.

Average = 0.34[latex]\cdot[/latex]2 + 0.19[latex]\cdot[/latex]2 + 0.22[latex]\cdot[/latex]2 + 0.08[latex]\cdot[/latex]3 + 0.17[latex]\cdot[/latex]3 = 2.25 bits. For 100 characters: 225 bits.

Answer: 225
